The daily field guide for digital media

AI Media Scout

2026-11-08 · All platforms · Open-source software

Today’s expanded edition covers 92 creative fields, adding game localization and stage lighting, with 789 configured repository queries and 22 model tasks. It contains 51 detailed guides and 185 additional eligible, license-screened discoveries awaiting full profiles. Sixteen guides complete earlier screened entries. Discovery includes recent, newly created and established work; there is no popularity cutoff or daily count quota. Current retained-catalog metadata, 1,187 additional repositories from today’s query union, 535 license-bearing metadata records and targeted source follow-ups were screened beyond the automatic README shortlist. Raw unreviewed and excluded candidates remain local; this is not a claim that every collected candidate was fully reviewed. All featured software grants were reviewed in full, with model weights, fonts/assets, paid services and required proprietary hosts separated. Every item has a dated assessment of licensing, results, setup, maintenance, independent use and dependencies. Unresolved evidence stays Quality unverified; explicit current prototype/instability reasons alone support Experimental. No discovered tool was installed/run, and no new tool is recommended merely for its stars, documentation, test totals or owner demo. Existing weekly library coverage was complete before collection; the new source reviews join that week and will be rechecked in the cumulative library. Verified collection: 789/789 repository queries attempted; 789 successful, 0 partial, 0 failed and 126 bounded/truncated. All 22 model tasks were attempted; 0 failed. These are bounded discovery attempts, not an exhaustive census or quality approval. Separate from successful search queries, 39 watchlist fetches and 3 enrichment attempts failed; the detailed warnings remain in the report. A 404/409 is an availability gap, not proof of abandonment or license revocation.

How it uses AI

A static browser application runs Real-ESRGAN upscaling and optional YuNet/RestoreFormer++ face restoration locally through ONNX Runtime Web. [1] [3]

Introduction

A static browser application runs Real-ESRGAN upscaling and optional YuNet/RestoreFormer++ face restoration locally through ONNX Runtime Web. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Private photo-upscaling studies with an adjustable restoration strength and a direct before/after comparison. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

Owner examples compare reduced source images with 4× reconstructions. The linked app was not accessible through the web-fetch tool in this review, so no live app test is claimed. [1] [3]

Install

Use a recent compatible browser and serve the cloned static files over local HTTP. There is no application build/backend dependency; model downloads are separate. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Use a recent compatible browser and serve the cloned static files over local HTTP. There is no application build/backend dependency; model downloads are separate.
git clone https://github.com/Dhee2211/HDify.git
cd HDify
python3 -m http.server 8000

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Open localhost:8000 and load a representative photo.
  2. Choose the enlargement and whether to restore detected faces; allow first-use model downloads.
  3. Compare source/output and reduce strength when restoration invents or smooths detail.
  4. Export and inspect identity, fine texture and tile boundaries at actual size.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3]

Hardware
No numeric GPU/RAM minimum is published. Downloads are about 67 MB for super-resolution, 0.2 MB detector and 71 MB face restoration on demand, with browser caching.
Software
Python 3 or another static server; README lists Chrome/Edge 113+ or Safari 26+ for WebGPU. A slower CPU fallback is described.
Platforms
Browser/driver dependent; a compatible browser interface does not prove all mobile or older GPU combinations work.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [2] [1] [3]

  • Weights: MIT app code. NOTICE lists separate BSD-3 Real-ESRGAN, Apache-2.0 RestoreFormer++ and MIT YuNet/ONNX components; review model/dataset terms separately, particularly for commercial face restoration.
  • Commercial: Software use follows MIT. MIT app code. NOTICE lists separate BSD-3 Real-ESRGAN, Apache-2.0 RestoreFormer++ and MIT YuNet/ONNX components; review model/dataset terms separately, particularly for commercial face restoration.
  • Cost: Local compute plus any chosen external model or service; provider access and charges are separate.

Why it merits attention

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1] [3]

Limitations

Output is capped near 64 megapixels, transparency is flattened to white and at most ten detected faces are processed. Small faces can be missed; generated detail is not recovered ground truth. [1] [3]

How it uses AI

A browser pipeline separates vocals, estimates pitch, applies an RVC voice model and remixes the converted voice with the instrumental. [1] [3]

Introduction

A browser pipeline separates vocals, estimates pitch, applies an RVC voice model and remixes the converted voice with the instrumental. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Local voice-conversion and cover experiments using recordings and voice models you are authorized to use. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The maintainer publishes workspace/result screenshots and one machine-specific timing. The live app URL was inaccessible to the research fetch tool; no playback or conversion was tested here. [1] [3]

Install

Use the linked app or clone, install npm dependencies and run the development server. Source development either needs weights/dist or the documented pinned remote model base URL in .env.local. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Use the linked app or clone, install npm dependencies and run the development server. Source development either needs weights/dist or the documented pinned remote model base URL in .env.local.
git clone https://github.com/ouor/rvc-webgpu.git
cd rvc-webgpu
npm install
npm run dev

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Load an authorized song, vocal recording or separated vocal/instrumental pair.
  2. Load the intended RVC model and optional index, then inspect conversion settings and pitch.
  3. Run separation/conversion and compare stems before remixing.
  4. Export WAV/MP3 or stems and listen carefully for artifacts and voice/likeness concerns.

Hardware & software

WebGPU browser. No universal native OS or mobile support matrix is documented.

Official input/output examples and a Gradio/CLI integration illustrate the method. They are owner research results, not proof that arbitrary portraits, materials or lighting match physically. [1]

Install

Create the documented Python 3.10 Conda/CUDA environment, clone the source and install requirements. Obtain the separate ControlNet and base-model weights, then launch the Gradio interface or follow simple_run.py. [1]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Create the documented Python 3.10 Conda/CUDA environment, clone the source and install requirements. Obtain the separate ControlNet and base-model weights, then launch the Gradio interface or follow simple_run.py.
git clone https://github.com/iamNCJ/DiLightNet
cd DiLightNet
pip install -r requirements.txt
python3 gradio_app.py

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Prepare a provisional image, foreground mask and compatible radiance hints.
  2. Load the provided NeuralTextureControlNet with its matching base-model pipeline.
  3. Change a controlled lighting parameter and compare results against the source subject.
  4. Treat background inpainting/provisional generation as separate stages and inspect consistency before compositing.

Hardware
Minimum system RAM, VRAM and total disk space are not documented in the reviewed instructions.
Software

CUDA-oriented setup. A Gradio page does not establish Apple Silicon, CPU-only or all-OS inference support.

The released neural component is the foreground stage, not every upstream/downstream generator. The conditioning tensor has a specific image/mask/radiance format; unsupported community models are not automatically compatible. The current full setup has not been independently reproduced here; use these as dated blocker reports rather than proof all inference routes fail. Independent user reports describe obtaining results, and primary comparison-paper search excerpts evaluate DiLightNet on defined relighting tasks. First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

Local agent-assisted post-production, title-sequence rendering and inspectable edits in DaVinci Resolve Studio. [1]

Install

Install the documented macOS prerequisites and licensed Resolve host, clone the repository, review the installer and run its normal route. Start the launcher after the local model downloads; the vision add-on is a separate optional installation. [1]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.

git clone https://github.com/willturner-maker/resolve-ai-workflow.git

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Confirm the local model server, dashboard and actual Resolve MCP connections.

  4. Compare the rendered result and state read-backs before using the full timeline; stop the stack with stop-resolve-ai.sh.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1]

Hardware
Maintainer recommends at least 48 GB unified memory, tuned on a 96 GB Mac. The initial language-model download is tens of GB; optional vision adds roughly 560 MB of environment and 52 MB of models. These are documented recommendations/sizes, not tested minima.
Software
macOS/Homebrew, Python 3.11+, Node 20+, Apple Silicon, Resolve Studio, local Splash model server and Blender for the title path. Optional vision uses its own Python 3.12 environment.
Platforms
Apple Silicon macOS workstation. Other OS and Intel Mac routes are not documented as equivalent.

Introduction

A local Electron studio uses language-model editing decisions, transcription and a video engine to turn long recordings into reviewed vertical clips with grounded hooks. [1]

What it is good for

Repurposing your own footage into short-form clips while keeping word-timed cuts, local export and an explicit review step. [1]

Demo & examples

Install

On macOS install Node 22.18+, FFmpeg, yt-dlp, whisper-cpp, Chrome/Chromium and Apple command-line tools. Clone, install the lockfile dependencies, run setup to fetch the local Whisper model, then start the app. [1]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. On macOS install Node 22.18+, FFmpeg, yt-dlp, whisper-cpp, Chrome/Chromium and Apple command-line tools. Clone, install the lockfile dependencies, run setup to fetch the local Whisper model, then start the app.
git clone https://github.com/gquthier/shorts-factory.git
cd shorts-factory
npm ci
npm run setup
npm start

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Open Démarrer and select either Anthropic API access or separately authenticated Claude CLI.
  2. Add audience/context and writing references, then import footage you can use.
  3. Transcribe, inspect candidate moments and hooks, render and check the clip.
  4. Export locally; publishing/analytics connections are optional and need separate accounts.

How it uses AI

An agent skill and utility set aligns explainer-animation events to actual narration keywords using forced alignment and frame-level checks. [1] [3] [4]

Introduction

An agent skill and utility set aligns explainer-animation events to actual narration keywords using forced alignment and frame-level checks. [1] [3] [4]

What it is good for

Narration-led educational animation in which visual emphasis should land on specific spoken words, including reuse of an existing voice recording. [1] [3] [4]

Demo & examples

Install

Place the complete project in the agent skills directory, install the utility requirements and run the documented doctor. Prepare the separately governed speech/alignment models and a Remotion project as needed. [1] [3] [4]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Place the complete project in the agent skills directory, install the utility requirements and run the documented doctor. Prepare the separately governed speech/alignment models and a Remotion project as needed.
git clone https://github.com/syydaniel/kazi ~/.claude/skills/kazi
cd ~/.claude/skills/kazi
pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python tools/doctor.py

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4]

  1. Supply a short script or your existing narration and a style reference.

  3. Have the agent build scenes whose key actions reference that table.
  4. Inspect a short preview, timing report, mix and final render; the timing score cannot judge visual design.

A native macOS video editor exposes timeline, effect, import, preview and export operations to an AI agent through its built-in MCP server. [1] [3]

Introduction

A native macOS video editor exposes timeline, effect, import, preview and export operations to an AI agent through its built-in MCP server. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Agent-assisted assembly and revision of editable video timelines with live updates in the native editor and frame previews. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

Install

Download the appropriate native DMG from official releases, or build native/ with Rust, Xcode, FFmpeg libraries and pkg-config. Use Connect AI in the projects page or register the rayna binary as a stdio MCP process. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Download the appropriate native DMG from official releases, or build native/ with Rust, Xcode, FFmpeg libraries and pkg-config. Use Connect AI in the projects page or register the rayna binary as a stdio MCP process.
git clone https://github.com/flaxodotdev/liemo.git
cd liemo/native
brew install ffmpeg pkgconf
cargo run --release

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Open or create a project and import representative local footage.

  3. Ask for one timeline edit, inspect the live result and undo/history.
  4. Render a preview frame and export; without the open app, MCP tools edit project files directly.

Introduction

An offline Mac concept-house designer uses a small local language model to interpret conversational briefs and edit requests, while deterministic geometry generates the drawings. [1]

What it is good for

Exploring room layouts, elevations, roof plans and printable architectural concept sets from a natural-language house brief. [1]

Demo & examples

The maintainer shows unedited generated plans and a concept-sheet set. These illustrate schematic output, not construction-ready design or professional validation. [1]

Install

On Apple Silicon with Python 3.10+ and Git, clone the source, create a virtual environment, install app/LLM extras, download the documented model and optionally create the local application bundle. [1]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. On Apple Silicon with Python 3.10+ and Git, clone the source, create a virtual environment, install app/LLM extras, download the documented model and optionally create the local application bundle.
git clone https://github.com/RyFinance/dreambuilt ~/DreamBuilt
cd ~/DreamBuilt
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[app,llm]"
.venv/bin/dreambuilt get-model
.venv/bin/python tools/make_app.py --install

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Launch the app and enter a brief specifying desired rooms, dimensions and style.
  2. Use the local LLM for chatty wording or named-room edit requests; a rule-based brief parser is also available.
  3. Compare revisions, adjust walls/room placement and inspect every floor relationship.
  4. Export the concept set for discussion with a qualified designer; do not use it as construction documents.

How it uses AI

A local Linux workbench combines neural segmentation, editable masks and linked 2D/3D scan visualization, with PNG and portable offline HTML exchange. [1] [3]

Introduction

A local Linux workbench combines neural segmentation, editable masks and linked 2D/3D scan visualization, with PNG and portable offline HTML exchange. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Research visualization and nonclinical anatomy/volume-media preparation from scans you are authorized to use, including corrected segmentation and shareable visual views. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

A synthetic exploration route is supplied, but it does not run AI models. Actual segmentation uses separately downloaded models; this is not clinical validation. [1] [3]

Install

On supported Linux install the documented system/build tools and Node, clone the project and run its CPU bootstrap. Check doctor and serve locally; configure/download the optional AI models separately before expecting real segmentation. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. On supported Linux install the documented system/build tools and Node, clone the project and run its CPU bootstrap. Check doctor and serve locally; configure/download the optional AI models separately before expecting real segmentation.
git clone https://github.com/Truth129/3DScan.git
cd 3DScan
scripts/bootstrap.sh --torch cpu
.venv/bin/scan3d doctor
.venv/bin/scan3d serve

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Open 127.0.0.1:9010 and inspect the synthetic demo first, keeping it distinct from inference.
  2. Import authorized scan data and select a separately configured segmentation task.
  3. Review/correct the masks in linked slices and 3D view.
  4. Export visual views/PNG/offline HTML with required notices; keep patient data out of public examples.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3]

Hardware
At least 16 GB RAM is documented. CPU installation about 3.5 GB, AMD route about 9 GB, plus separate weights/cases. GPU optional; larger volumes/jobs can require much more.
Software
Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.28+, Git/curl, C++ compiler, CMake, pkg-config, OpenJPEG/zlib development packages and Node 22.12+. Bootstrap provisions Python 3.14. Reviewed browser route is Chrome/Chromium/Edge with WebGL2.
Platforms
Linux. macOS/Windows are explicitly unsupported and arm64 is untested.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [2] [1] [3]

  • Weights: Apache-2.0 original code. nnInteractive weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; some TotalSegmentator tasks require separate/noncommercial permissions; MRSegmentator model grant is not separately clarified in the reviewed summary. Code licensing does not clear all model use.
  • Commercial: Software use follows Apache-2.0. Apache-2.0 original code. nnInteractive weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; some TotalSegmentator tasks require separate/noncommercial permissions; MRSegmentator model grant is not separately clarified in the reviewed summary. Code licensing does not clear all model use.
  • Cost: Local compute plus any chosen external model or service; provider access and charges are separate.

Why it merits attention

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1] [3]

Limitations

Research visualization only; the tool is not a diagnostic device. Synthetic demo, optional MRI and actual CT inference are different scopes. Large datasets can exceed the stated baseline and a browser UI does not make the host portable. [1] [3]

How it uses AI

A browser notebook builder prepares editable Colab workflows for MiniMax H3 video/audio generation, preset selection, reference images and compatible LoRAs. [1] [3]

Introduction

A browser notebook builder prepares editable Colab workflows for MiniMax H3 video/audio generation, preset selection, reference images and compatible LoRAs. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Preparing and inspecting a cloud-GPU video-generation notebook without a local inference GPU, including text/first-frame/reference routes. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The current status limits confirmed GPU success to the original Turbo 8 route at 864×480. Refactored runtime, larger default and live Drive integration have not received equivalent end-to-end validation. [1] [3]

Install

Open the official builder or Colab notebook, save a copy in your account and choose the required high-RAM A100 runtime. Select a preset before running setup cells; inspect exported notebooks before execution. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Open the official builder or Colab notebook, save a copy in your account and choose the required high-RAM A100 runtime. Select a preset before running setup cells; inspect exported notebooks before execution.

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Select text-to-video or the appropriate image/reference preset and export/copy the notebook.
  2. Allocate the documented runtime and confirm memory/storage checks.
  3. Run setup cells in order, then supply the prompt and any runtime-accessible image in the generation cell.
  4. Preview/download output, distinguish temporary runtime storage from Drive, and disconnect/delete the cloud runtime when done.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3]

Hardware
Notebook checks at least 38,000 MiB GPU memory and 48 GiB system RAM; allow 50 GB free storage for one model set. The Turbo set is about 44.4 GB; keeping the other diffusion family adds about 20.96 GB.
Software
Google Colab account with suitable A100/high-RAM allocation, ComfyUI/notebook dependencies and model downloads. The optional legacy Windows x64 companion only prepares/uploads notebooks.
Platforms
Browser-based builder/Colab; optional Windows x64 companion. No local Windows/macOS/Linux inference parity or free-tier guarantee is claimed.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [2] [1] [3]

  • Weights: MIT builder/notebook code. MiniMax H3 weights, Turbo LoRAs and ComfyUI have separate terms; access or commercial/geographic eligibility is not granted by this repository.
  • Commercial: Software use follows MIT. MIT builder/notebook code. MiniMax H3 weights, Turbo LoRAs and ComfyUI have separate terms; access or commercial/geographic eligibility is not granted by this repository.
  • Cost: Builder is free. Suitable Colab compute, model access and storage can cost money; no free GPU allocation is promised.

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1] [3]

How it uses AI

A local MCP image server lets an AI agent execute explicit image conversions, crops, metadata removal, contact-style merges and thumbnails through a structured tool interface. [1] [3] [4]

Introduction

A local MCP image server lets an AI agent execute explicit image conversions, crops, metadata removal, contact-style merges and thumbnails through a structured tool interface. [1] [3] [4]

What it is good for

Agent-directed preparation of image assets, including HEIC input conversion and metadata-clean thumbnail production on local files. [1] [3] [4]

Demo & examples

The package README supplies an example agent sequence and file-handling contract. This assesses the AI-facing MCP workflow; the underlying image transforms are deterministic. [1] [3] [4]

Install

With Node 24+, register the npx-launched stdio server in the MCP client and restart the host. No separate model weights are supplied by this package. [1] [3] [4]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. With Node 24+, register the npx-launched stdio server in the MCP client and restart the host. No separate model weights are supplied by this package.
claude mcp add dryplate -- npx -y @dryplate/mcp

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4]

  1. Give the agent an absolute or home-relative source-file path; an attached image is not automatically a server-side file.
  2. Request a concrete transform such as metadata removal followed by a thumbnail.
  3. Inspect the new suffixed files and output format; existing files are preserved unless explicit overwrite is requested.
  4. Check the actual metadata, image quality and dimensions before using the asset.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3] [4]

Hardware
Minimum system RAM, VRAM and total disk space are not documented in the reviewed instructions.
Software
Node.js 24+, npx and an MCP client running stdio processes. The Node transform path uses sharp; browser SDK codecs are a different route.
Platforms
Claude Code/Desktop are documented tested clients. A full native OS and codec compatibility matrix is not documented.

  • Commercial: Software use follows MIT. MIT project code; the SDK ships an unmodified libheif WASM binary under LGPL-3.0 with separate notices. The external AI client/model and input assets have separate terms.
  • Cost: Local compute plus any chosen external model or service; provider access and charges are separate.

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1] [3] [4]

How it uses AI

A game-text localization pipeline integrates model-assisted translation, SQLite translation memory, deterministic QA, human revision and reproducible preview/release artifacts. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Introduction

A game-text localization pipeline integrates model-assisted translation, SQLite translation memory, deterministic QA, human revision and reproducible preview/release artifacts. [1] [3] [4] [5]

What it is good for

Maintaining authorized localization across game updates while tracing changed strings, human fixes and reusable translation-memory entries. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Demo & examples

The maintainer traces the framework to recurring Mir Tankov localization and provides an example project. That is owner provenance, not independent end-to-end validation for other games. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Install

Clone the source and use a Python 3.10+ virtual environment. Install the selected extras, validate and scan the example without a translation key, then copy the complete example and configure your actual resources/provider. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Clone the source and use a Python 3.10+ virtual environment. Install the selected extras, validate and scan the example without a translation key, then copy the complete example and configure your actual resources/provider.
git clone https://github.com/AllenXiao95/Game-Localizer.git
cd Game-Localizer
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[all]"
.venv/bin/localizer validate-config projects/example/project.yaml
.venv/bin/localizer scan projects/example/project.yaml

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3] [4] [5]

  1. Copy the example project and set source/target languages, adapter globs and separate workspace/output/TM paths.
  2. Configure an OpenAI-compatible translation endpoint and environment credential; replace placeholder tokenizer settings.
  3. Run a preview build, inspect QA and revise strings in the loopback dashboard.
  4. Rebuild incrementally, review in-game output and use a release artifact only after its quality gate passes; publishing is a separate authorized operation.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1] [3] [4] [5]

Hardware
Minimum system RAM, VRAM and total disk space are not documented in the reviewed instructions.
Software
Python 3.10+, Git and a compatible translation endpoint for inference. Optional Transformers tokenizer, AES archive and remote-publishing extras are conditional dependencies.
Platforms
Windows PowerShell and macOS/Linux virtual-environment routes are documented. Hardware/model requirements depend on the selected external endpoint.

How it uses AI

A Python CLI/library uses configurable AI providers for game-text translation and three-pass proofreading, with checkpoints, protected tags and format/font/layout validation. [1] [3]

Introduction

A Python CLI/library uses configurable AI providers for game-text translation and three-pass proofreading, with checkpoints, protected tags and format/font/layout validation. [1] [3]

What it is good for

Batch localization of exported game resources while preserving placeholders and reviewing dialogue-box, glyph and byte constraints. [1] [3]

Demo & examples

The official README demonstrates a Unity-style JSON configuration and the complete translation/proofreading/export sequence. No independent verified game release was established in this review. [1] [3]

Install

Install the current PyPI package with Python 3.11+ through uv or pip. Initialize gameloc.toml, configure resource formats/languages and a provider, then inspect a dry-run before translation. [1] [3]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Install the current PyPI package with Python 3.11+ through uv or pip. Initialize gameloc.toml, configure resource formats/languages and a provider, then inspect a dry-run before translation.
pip install gameloc
gameloc init
gameloc status
gameloc translate --dry-run

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1] [3]

  1. Point the TOML source definition at authorized JSON/JSONL/CSV/TSV/PO resources and set the target language.
  2. Select a supported API, local compatible endpoint or CLI provider and configure its access.
  3. Translate with checkpointing, then run proofread prepare, run and export.
  4. Export to copies of the game files and inspect actual in-game text, tags and layout.

How it uses AI

A Chromium extension combines calmer YouTube browsing with optional on-device or user-configured AI video summaries for media research. [1]

Introduction

A Chromium extension combines calmer YouTube browsing with optional on-device or user-configured AI video summaries for media research. [1]

What it is good for

Surveying reference videos by actual frames and concise content summaries instead of relying only on promotional thumbnails/titles. [1]

Demo & examples

The owner supplies before/after screenshots. The frame/title replacement is deterministic; only the optional summary route is the AI capability assessed here. [1]

Install

Use the linked official Chrome Web Store release, or load the source directory unpacked through the browser extensions page. Configure a supported on-device or own-key/local summary provider separately. [1]

  1. Obtain the official source or release linked below.
  2. Use the linked official Chrome Web Store release, or load the source directory unpacked through the browser extensions page. Configure a supported on-device or own-key/local summary provider separately.
git clone https://github.com/sub8u/honest-thumbnails.git

First project

Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch. [1]

  1. Enable the extension and select a frame/title-card style.
  2. Choose and test the optional summary provider in settings.
  3. Request a small set of summaries and check whether each used captions or only a description.
  4. Follow through to the video and verify source claims; a sampled frame or summary can omit important content.

Hardware & software

Requirements below are documented for this workflow. Unspecified limits are not inferred. [1]

Hardware
Minimum system RAM, VRAM and total disk space are not documented in the reviewed instructions.
Software
A supported Chromium-family browser. Built-in AI availability depends on Chrome version/hardware; own-provider routes need separately configured API or local-model access.
Platforms
Chrome, Edge, Brave and Arc are listed. A minimum OS/RAM/VRAM matrix for built-in AI is not documented in the project README.

License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Model weights, assets and services remain separate. [2] [1]

  • Weights: MIT code; bundled typeface is OFL. YouTube, optional SponsorBlock data and the chosen AI endpoint retain their own terms. Summaries leave the device only when an external endpoint is selected, per the maintainer.
  • Commercial: Software use follows MIT. MIT code; bundled typeface is OFL. YouTube, optional SponsorBlock data and the chosen AI endpoint retain their own terms. Summaries leave the device only when an external endpoint is selected, per the maintainer.
  • Cost: Free extension code; optional external inference and local model resources are separate.

Why it merits attention

Included for the documented creative workflow. A complete guide and popularity do not establish output reliability. [1]

Limitations

Blocked captions can reduce a summary to description-only input; automatically sampled frames can be blank/intros. This is a media-research aid, not an image-generation tool or factual authenticity guarantee. Bundled Instrument Serif is OFL; optional SponsorBlock data has separate community database terms. Neither is relicensed by the extension MIT grant. [1] [5]

  • rouges78/GameStringer · excluded: The current custom Source-Available License explicitly differs from OSI open source; public builds and AI translation features do not change the grant. Source
  • zenyrae123/Charakuru · excluded: The current custom source-available terms restrict commercial/business use and redistribution and explicitly are not an OSI software grant. Source
  • AryaVora621/agentcad · excluded: The full PolyForm Noncommercial software grant restricts commercial use; paid commercial terms do not make that public grant open source. Source
  • galact-byte/game-loc-kit · excluded: The current software grant is custom source-available with commercial authorization requirements; earlier MIT rights are not a grant for the current source. Source
  • TechsOneAi/ComposeLintAI · needs-license-review: The complete purported Apache text changes operative definition/disclaimer wording. Metadata and a license badge do not establish the standard grant; held for clarification. Source
  • PrinceEagle/Formula-to-Nodes · needs-license-review: The Blender listing establishes the creative AI/MCP concept, but the complete official root-license request returned 404; no OSI grant is approved from the listing alone. Source
  • berkeflz-real/Cyberpunk-Mod-Translator · needs-license-review: The retained license notice describes WolvenKit GPL terms but does not grant a software license for the translator’s own code; held pending an actual grant. Source
